summary: No thesis is broken by evidence in the files. There were no fills, stop_alerts is empty and every stop block reads ok. The PM's L7 review in close.json found DPZ and SAM still on the menu, DPZ with CFO above net income, and no guidance-cut or negative 8-K on any holding. The account ended at $617.91 (+2.99% since inception against SPY -6.50%) with about half the book in cash because the regime filter is off. None of the Reviewer's lessons (L2-L10) names the fundamentals-analyst, and learning.json has no graded calls for me, so no lesson shaped this review.
update: Fundamentals read on each holding, using only what close.json stores. (1) DPZ, about 12.0% of equity and the largest single name: the measurable clauses (on the menu, CFO $792M above net income $602M) hold. Two caveats stay open. Its top-of-sector rank is partly the wholesale-groceries SIC mislabel, and it fails leverage_not_up. The BNP Underperform ($295 PT) and the EVP sale are sentiment, not accounting evidence. The new $335 stop is 7.9% under the $361.53 mark, the third-closest stop after TLT (7.8%) and SAM (8.2%). (2) SAM: F8, CFO $270M against net income $108M, so cash backing is strong. Net income is thin, though, and the FY2025 statements predate the 2026 quarters and the 11-23 CEO handover. The fy_end staleness is the main accounting caveat. The 11-19 8-K 5.02 closes unread around 11-26/27. The menu clause is the one to check against the next screen. That sell-candidate status (L8) belongs to the Proposer and PM; nothing in my lane breaks the thesis. (3) KR: F7 with two failed tests (roa_improved, current_ratio_improved), the weakest score among the held names. Its CFO of $7.31B against net income of $1.02B is the strongest cash backing in the book. Its next fundamentals evidence is the company-confirmed 12-03 report, now inside the 5-day window. (4) The Staples bucket by business (KR and SAM) is about 8.3% of equity. Adding DPZ by SIC label makes it about 20.3%. Only the 8.3% figure reflects the businesses. (5) IDXX (F8, CFO $1,181.8M against net income $1,059.5M) and INCY (F8, CFO $1,413.5M against $1,286.7M) are intact. Together they are about 6.6% of equity in Health Care. INCY's MAESTRA-3 drop is a pipeline matter, not an accounting one. (6) MSCI is intact. It shares DPZ's leverage_not_up failure, and its Industrials SIC label is an artifact (the business is financial data). (7) CARG (gp_sector_pct 1.0, CFO about 1.9x net income) is intact. (8) VRSN (9/9, gp_sector_pct 0.993) is intact. There is one wording gap: its invalidation names 'the guidance raise was reversed', but the stored thesis never states that a guidance raise happened. That makes the clause hard to check, and the PM may want to restate it under L6. 'Top-ranked quality name on the screen' is also a rank claim that can go stale, like CARG's old 'Rank 2'. (9) TLT is an ETF outside the fundamentals screen, so I have no comment. Watch next run: whether SAM and DPZ stay on the menu, any fy_end rollover for SAM or KR, and KR's 12-03 print.
